facts:
## CELL FACTS

Cell 水_正财 (Water carrying The Steward). Persona The Steward (正财). Definition line: "Methodical, directed acquisition, the value built and kept". Keyword Caution, charge gentle, poles catalyst Security / friction Hoarding. Family function: Action. Cost dimension: value built and kept; counting what others spend freely. Arena: granary, kept things, stone by stone, seasons of saving. Classical portrait: methodical, directed acquisition; value built and kept; caution, thrift, the slow ledger. Ruled domains: Wealth, Savings, Steady love. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 偏财.
Element arena: Water (depth, current, tide, rain, spring, flow). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Earth. structural_interaction seed: "Earth directing Water cross-polarity — stability containing depth into productive form".
- k2_overview: "Your Water moves as the Steward: current disciplined into irrigation. You manage flows, income streams, schedules, family logistics, with the calm of a well-run canal. Nothing floods, nothing dries. It is unglamorous mastery, and every life around you runs smoother because your channels hold."
- k2_functional: "You administer gracefully: systems, budgets, routines that run without drought."
- adj_chips: {"catalyst":["Careful","Steady-flowing","Well-prepared"],"friction":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Wealth":"Your wealth is flow-managed: salaries channeled, streams diversified, leaks found early. You prosper by routing, not risking. Map the canals once a year and fortune stays irrigated.","Savings":"You save in reservoirs: automatic diversions filling quiet pools. Name each pool’s purpose, storm, harvest, joy, and the discipline becomes drinkable.","Steady love":"You love in reliable supply: presence delivered daily, needs anticipated, storms weathered by good infrastructure. Choose someone who notices plumbing. Then surprise the schedule occasionally. Even canals enjoy weather."}

  - row 0: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 1: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 2: [REDACTED: the target row]
- Sibling cell 水_偏财 chips (nothing you write may fit the sibling): {"catalyst":["Far-flowing","Adaptive","Magnetic"],"friction":["Up and down","Ungrounded","Everywhere at once"]}
- Sibling cell 水_偏财 friction row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "Your fortunes rise and fall on currents you ride but never steer. The windfall month, the wipeout quarter, the rescue that arrives from nowhere, the loss that follows it out: your financial life reads like a tide chart with no moon to blame."

Core element Earth, energy element Water. Law: Earth tames Water (土克水: banks give the river its path). Relative to the core the energy is the tamed, so Water is this core's Action. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Earth core that shows Water on the friction pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The friction pole of Water as the Action is the Underfueled band's case (the core burns more than it takes in); tone by pole: reminder. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. The pair cell 土_水's definition and advice for this pole are rewritten in the same batch (the pair skeleton) and are withheld here; no four-word run may be shared with them, so keep every phrase the ledger's own.

value.text: You hold money back long after holding it back makes sense. Having it in the pool feels safer than having it out, so you hold it rather than use it. Remember that money held back is only safe until the day it is needed.

value_b.text: Holding money back never feels like a choice to you. An untouched account feels like the point of earning, and you would rather watch it grow than let any go. If you hold it all back, you have earned money that never works for you.

value.text: Even with the people closest to you, you hold back first and help second. You would rather keep the account whole than give the full amount asked. For each amount you hold back from them, you take a little ease out of the closeness.

value.text: You count the cost before you let yourself want anything. Knowing the price makes a thing safe, so you count what a dinner costs ahead of what it is worth. Until you count the worth as well, you pay for every dinner without enjoying it.

value_b.text: Counting is how you decide what is allowed. You add up every cost before every pleasure, and you trust the total more than the wanting. You end up with a correct total and few of the things the money was for.

value.text: Being caught short is the thing counting every cost protects you from. You would rather know what a kindness costs than take it, and you count the free ones too. Notice that counting has a price too, paid in closeness you never let in.

value.text: You wait for the sure thing, and it rarely comes on time. Being certain means more to you than being early, so you wait past the moment for yes. Waiting to be certain, you lose the years a yes would already have given you.

value_b.text: To you, waiting too long feels like the careful choice. You would rather miss a chance than take a wrong one, and the ones you miss were mostly fine. Sooner or later you find that waiting costs more than a wrong yes would.

value.text: Waiting too long keeps you from being wrong. You want the sure yes more than the early one, and you wait until the choice makes itself. Do not forget that the price of waiting is the deals and people that stopped waiting for you.

value.text: No matter how close the person asking, you wait to be sure. You put being certain ahead of being there, and you leave them holding the question. By the time you stop waiting, you have already taken the time they needed to plan.
